title: The Orchard Signal
short: A false frost warning sends a fictional research crew searching for a bad reading.
brief: At a fictional orchard monitoring demonstration outside Tieton, a prototype data screen suddenly reported a hard frost even though other instruments recorded mild conditions. Volunteers worry that someone altered the dataset. Examine sensor location, temperature trends, timestamps, and cable labels to determine what actually happened.
caseQuestion: Which person reconfigured the sensor, and what created the misleading frost warning?

sites.label: Digital frost-warning display

clues.title: Split temperature chart
clues.detail: The public channel abruptly changes from 8°C to -4°C, while an independent nearby channel remains at 8°C. An abrupt single-channel change suggests inspecting the instrument.
clues.question: What should be checked first?
options: The spelling of a visitor name

clues.title: Alert screenshot
clues.detail: The automatic alert reads FROST because the prototype rule triggers below 0°C. It does not verify outdoor conditions independently.
clues.question: What does the alert actually establish?
options: The displayed sensor reading crossed a threshold

clues.title: Cold chamber note
clues.detail: The insulated test chamber is labeled -4°C TARGET. The probe wire runs out through a protected opening to the kiosk.
clues.question: Which explanation fits the dashboard change?
options: A chamber sensor appearing as an outdoor sensor

clues.title: Reference reading
clues.detail: At 5:05, a handheld reference thermometer reads 8°C. Its calibration is recorded separately.
clues.question: What supports checking the frost alarm?

clues.title: Cable marker B
clues.detail: A cable-tag photograph shows OUTDOOR-B before the probe move. The kiosk software continued calling that cable an outdoor reading.
clues.question: What caused the label conflict?
options: A physical move without a software label update
The cable was a different color

clues.title: Change-log gap
clues.detail: The official device log contains no entry for relocating sensor B. A handwritten personal note mentions a comparison test.
clues.question: What was missing?

clues.title: Timestamp match
clues.detail: The personal test note begins at 5:00, the same minute the public chart abruptly drops. The sequence and cable evidence agree.
clues.question: What does the matching time strengthen?
options: A connection between the test and the alert
A claim that a storm struck

labs.title: Cooling probe model
labs.story: Vary chamber temperature in a simplified sensor response model.
labs.explanation: A sensor reads its immediate environment, not an entire geographic region.
labs.question: Which scientific interpretation is best supported by this model?
options: Sensor location matters when interpreting a reading.
Every sensor reading describes the entire valley.

labs.title: Sensor delay model
labs.story: Vary an illustrative response lag and compare time to update.
labs.explanation: Slower update settings create longer displayed response times.
labs.question: Which scientific interpretation is best supported by this model?
options: Higher lag increases response time in this model.

labs.title: Alarm threshold
labs.story: Change the threshold and examine when the example alert would activate.
labs.explanation: Alerts follow configured rules; they must be interpreted with sensor placement.
labs.question: Which scientific interpretation is best supported by this model?
options: A configured threshold changes when an alert occurs.

math.prompt: The outdoor reference is 8°C and the chamber probe reads -4°C. What is the absolute difference?
math.hint: Find the distance between -4 and +8 on a number line.

events.label: Probe B moved for a test

explanation: The technician moved the connected probe to a cooled demonstration chamber and failed to update the shared display label. Independent data and timing show a misleading sensor label, not proof of an actual frost.

witnesses.name: Amir Solis
witnesses.statement: I worked with a comparison chamber near the display during the same period as the alert. I was testing how the probe responded.
witnesses.followup: I assumed the software names would be checked during final review.
witnesses.question: What log would help test Amir’s explanation of the alert?
options: Probe assignment and chamber test times
A photo of the fruit stand

witnesses.name: Piper Holt
witnesses.statement: I was preparing the evening forecast slides from the public dashboard. I did not visit the test enclosure.
witnesses.followup: When the chart jumped, I asked for a second thermometer.
witnesses.question: What step in Piper’s story is sound scientific practice?
options: Rely only on the first alarm
Assume every alert describes all orchards

witnesses.name: Sasha Liu
witnesses.statement: I walked the demonstration rows with visitors and photographed the display.
witnesses.followup: The outdoor thermometer showed 8°C in one image.
witnesses.question: Which independent observation does Sasha offer?
options: A weather prediction for next year
The name of a maintenance supplier

witnesses.name: Cal Rios
witnesses.statement: I carried cable clips to the equipment table and then closed the tool kit.
witnesses.followup: The probe wire was labeled B before the demonstration.
witnesses.question: What item could verify Cal’s cable-label recollection?
options: The color of the weather presenter’s coat

note: Entirely fictional educational case using a real regional place name as setting. No actual person, facility, business, incident, or allegation is represented.
